analysis:
Examined base ProviderLoop.swift lines 1-1178 (units 2-4) and the head patch, which only adds stored state at head lines 484-497. The new state covers add-on holds: AddonHoldBook, a hold task with a generation counter, a lease monitor task, an AddonIPCServer (a new local socket), AddonHoldPaths, and test seams. The seams are a paths override, an AddonIPCServer.Authenticate peer-authenticator override, a wall-clock closure and a drain timeout.

No behavior is visible in this unit; the logic lives in ProviderLoop+AddonHold, AddonIPCServer and AddonHoldBook, which were not supplied. This adds new local attack surface at the TB-003 operator-vs-process boundary, similar to the fan-helper TB-010 and T-044 lease impersonation pattern. A local process that can reach the socket could trigger drain-and-unload of models. That would be a DoS of serving (T-029, T-010) or interference with the serving lifecycle.

Integration must verify the following:
(1) Socket path permissions and peer authentication, including code-signing or audit-token checks rather than the PID alone. Confirm the production authenticator is non-nil and not bypassable, and that addonPeerAuthenticatorOverride is reachable only from tests.
(2) A hold cannot leave admission closed indefinitely; leases expire via the monitor, and the wall-clock addonHoldNowMs is not manipulable by local clock changes.
(3) A hold or unload does not bypass the self-test or weight-hash state (failedSelfTestHashes, liveModelHashes), and does not re-advertise models.
(4) No prompt or plaintext data, keys or authorization state (A-001, A-003, A-016) are exposed over the IPC.
(5) Paths do not resolve into user-writable locations that are followed with symlinks.
(6) Whether the threat model needs a new boundary or threat entry for the add-on IPC.

No concrete regression can be cited from the stored declarations alone.
